---
title: "Bet selection and staking"
subtitle: "Paper 6 in a series on UK All-Weather racing outcomes"
author: "Patrick Gillen"
date: "2026-09-09"
abstract: |
  Papers 1 to 5 changed the model and left the betting rule alone: back the
  horse whose model win probability clears 0.15 and whose model-to-market
  ratio clears 1.3, one unit a bet. That rule is Owen's, inherited from a
  different dataset, and it has never been examined. This paper changes it
  and nothing else. The model is held fixed at paper 5's encoder.
  Nine selection rules and three staking rules are searched on paper 5's
  held-out validation slice — 1,505 races the fit that scores them never saw
  — in two stages, selection first at a flat stake and staking second on
  whatever selection won. One rule per bet type was declared mechanically,
  behind an eligibility gate that counts bets placed rather than races
  selected, and frozen before any test contact. The test split was then
  scored once.
  **Both stages declared the incumbent, for all three bet types.** Searched
  out of sample, no alternative selection and no alternative stake beats
  Owen's rule. The remaining question is the control: against backing the
  market favourite flat — a rule with no model in it — the incumbent is
  `r local({ S <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj")), "_targets_p6"); c <- targets::tar_read(p6_test_contrasts, store = S); r <- c[c$bet == "win" & grepl("incumbent", c$question), ]; sprintf("%+.1f points on the win market, 90%% interval [%+.1f, %+.1f]", 100 * r$diff_point, 100 * r$ci_lo, 100 * r$ci_hi) })`
  and
  `r local({ S <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj")), "_targets_p6"); c <- targets::tar_read(p6_test_contrasts, store = S); r <- c[c$bet == "place" & grepl("incumbent", c$question), ]; sprintf("%+.1f points on the place market, [%+.1f, %+.1f]", 100 * r$diff_point, 100 * r$ci_lo, 100 * r$ci_hi) })`.
  Three of four such contrasts contain zero; the place market is the
  exception and favours the model. Every arm loses money at real starting
  prices, and priced at a zero-margin book the incumbent is roughly
  break-even on the win market — so the loss is the over-round, and closing
  it needs a better price rather than a better rule.
format:
  html: default
  pdf:
    toc: true
    number-sections: true
bibliography: references.bib

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(targets)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

# Paper 6 reads the paper-6 store. Like papers 4 and 5 and unlike papers 1-3
# this does NOT call tar_config_set(): that writes the project-root
# `_targets.yaml`, which papers 1-3's own setup chunks also write, and
# pointing it at `_targets_p6` would send their next render at the wrong
# store. Passing `store =` per call leaves `_targets.yaml` untouched.
P6_ROOT  <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj"))
P6_STORE <- file.path(P6_ROOT, "_targets_p6")

# Sourced robustly across the cwd tar_quarto() sets (project root) and the
# one a direct render would set (this folder).
source(file.path(P6_ROOT, "papers", "06_betting_strategy", "_helpers.R"))

# Every target the section files read is loaded here, centrally, so
# tar_quarto()'s dependency detection sees them: files pulled in with
# {{< include >}} are not scanned.
tar_load(c(p6_search_set_check, p6_universe, p6_fit_provenance_tbl,
           p6_ledger_gate, p6_positions,
           p6_price_coverage_val, p6_overround_val,
           p6_field_sizes_val, p6_field_sizes_test,
           p6_eachway_terms_decision,
           p6_thresholds_val, p6_thresholds_test, p6_contrast_check,
           p6_stage_a_grid, p6_stage_a_contrasts, p6_stage_b_grid,
           p6_gate_demonstration, p6_val_incumbent,
           p6_declaration, p6_declaration_frozen, p6_declared_rules_file,
           p6_test_arms, p6_test_selection_sizes, p6_test_results,
           p6_test_contrasts, p6_margin_decomposition,
           p6_fig_cumulative, p6_fig_val_vs_test, p6_test_report_file),
         store = P6_STORE)

n_val_races  <- p6_universe$n_val_races
n_test_races <- p6_universe$n_test_races
n_fit_races  <- p6_search_set_check$n_races_fit
```
